nations.name: Hla'alua
nations.lands: Taoyuan and Namaxia districts, Kaohsiung City, Taiwan

facts.text: In 2014 the Hla'alua were officially recognized as a distinct people, becoming the 15th Indigenous people listed in Taiwan.
The Hla'alua are formed by four communities, Paiciana, Vilanganʉ, Talicia and Hlihlara, in Kaohsiung City.

nations.name: Ainu
nations.lands: Hokkaido and other parts of Japan

facts.text: Upopoy, a national centre for Ainu history and culture in Shiraoi, Hokkaido, opened to the public in July 2020.

source.title: About Upopoy
source.publisher: Upopoy National Ainu Museum and Park

facts.text: A 2019 Japanese law names the Ainu as an Indigenous people of northern Japan, especially Hokkaido, and aims for a society that respects Ainu pride.

source.title: Act on Promoting Measures to Achieve a Society in which the Pride of Ainu People is Respected (Act No. 16 of 2019)
source.publisher: Japanese Law Translation, Ministry of Justice, Japan

nations.name: Sherpa
nations.lands: Solukhumbu and the upper Dudh Koshi and Sun Koshi valleys of northeastern Nepal, from Solu to Helambu, and Kathmandu

facts.text: Sherpa communities use a customary system called nawa to look after crops and forests.

source.title: शेर्पा (Sherpa)
source.publisher: National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities, Nepal

facts.text: In Nepal's 2021 census, 90.3 percent of Sherpa people reported Sherpa as their own language.

source.title: शेर्पा (Sherpa)
source.publisher: National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities, Nepal

nations.name: Pangcah
nations.lands: East of the Central Mountain Range in Hualien and Taitung counties, plus the Hengchun Peninsula, Taiwan

facts.text: Their own name, Pangcah, means people and kinsmen. The name Amis came from neighbours in Taitung and was later adopted by scholars.
In some Pangcah communities, each age class takes its name from a key event of its time, so one class name marks the computer era.

nations.name: Karen
nations.lands: Eastern Myanmar, including Karen State, and western and northern Thailand

facts.text: Karen is a name for several related peoples who speak 12 related Karenic languages; about 85 percent of Karen belong to the S'gaw or Pwo branches.
Karen communities have lived in what is now northern Thailand for many centuries.

nations.name: Bodo
nations.lands: Bodoland Territorial Region and other parts of Assam, India

facts.text: Bodo is an associate official language of Assam, and in 2022 the state announced it would become a medium of instruction in Classes XI and XII.

source.title: CM Dr. Sarma attends 61st Annual conference of Bodo Sahitya Sabha (Press Release No. 129/2022)
source.publisher: Directorate of Information and Public Relations, Government of Assam

facts.text: Bodo is one of the 22 languages listed in the Eighth Schedule of India's Constitution.

source.title: Languages Included in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution
source.publisher: Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs, India

nations.name: Ibaloi
nations.lands: Southern Benguet and the Baguio area in northern Luzon, Philippines

facts.text: The Ibaloi are one of the three major ethnolinguistic groups of Benguet province, with the Kankanaey and Kalanguya.
Benguet's official provincial fruit is a native blueberry whose Ibaloi name is ayosip.

nations.name: Tripura
nations.lands: Chittagong Hill Tracts and other districts of Bangladesh, and the state of Tripura, India

facts.text: Tripura University opened a Department of Kokborok in 2015 and began doctoral research in the language in 2018.
Kokborok, the Tripura language, has been an official language of the Indian state of Tripura since 1979.

nations.name: Magar
nations.lands: Hills of the Rapti and Gandaki river basins in western and central Nepal, and communities across Nepal

facts.text: Magar communities keep customary institutions such as the bheja, and each year they choose a mukhiya as community leader, who settles small disputes.

source.title: मगर (Magar)
source.publisher: National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities, Nepal

facts.text: In 2021 Nepal's Language Commission recommended Magar as an official language for both Gandaki and Karnali provinces.

source.title: Language Commission recommends province-wise official languages before government

nations.name: Tamu
nations.lands: Tamuwan, the hills between the Trishuli and Kali Gandaki rivers in central Nepal, including Gorkha, Lamjung, Kaski, Syangja, Manang and Mustang

facts.text: In 2021 Nepal's Language Commission recommended Gurung, the Tamu language, as an official language of Gandaki Province.

source.title: Language Commission recommends province-wise official languages before government

facts.text: Tamu Kyui, the Tamu language, now has its own Khema script, which Nepal's Language Commission has recognized.

source.title: गुरुङ(तमू) (Gurung, Tamu)
source.publisher: National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities, Nepal

nations.name: Kalasha
nations.lands: The Kalasha valleys of Bamburet, Birir and Rumbur in the Hindu Kush, Chitral, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan

facts.text: Kalasha families use Suri Jagek to choose the right time to sow seeds and care for livestock, and to anticipate natural hazards.
Suri Jagek is practiced at local observatories in three Kalasha valley villages: Bamburet, Birir and Rumbur.

source.title: Pakistan's first independent nomination Suri Jagek inscribed by UNESCO (PR No. 04)
source.publisher: Press Information Department, Government of Pakistan

nations.name: Sakizaya
nations.lands: Hualien Plain, the East Rift Valley and coast, Taiwan

facts.text: Through a cultural revival led by the community itself, the Sakizaya were recognized as one of Taiwan's Indigenous peoples in 2007.
The Sakizaya population was about 985 in January 2020.

nations.name: Kankanaey
nations.lands: Benguet and Mountain Province in the Cordillera of northern Luzon, Philippines

facts.text: The Kankanaey are one of the three major ethnolinguistic groups of Benguet province, with the Ibaloi and Kalanguya.
Benguet's official provincial fruit is a native blueberry, known in Kankanaey as gotmo or alumani.

nations.name: Ifugao
nations.lands: Ifugao Province in the Cordillera mountains of northern Luzon, Philippines

facts.text: Ifugao families still farm and care for their mountain rice terraces, a UNESCO World Heritage living landscape since 1995.

source.title: Rice Terraces of the Philippine Cordilleras

facts.text: The Hudhud, long narrative chants of the Ifugao sung at rice sowing and harvest, are on UNESCO's list of intangible heritage.

nations.name: Tao
nations.lands: Lanyu (Orchid Island), Taitung County, Taiwan

facts.text: The people call themselves Tao, meaning human, while Yami is the name used officially.
The Tao, who live on Lanyu, also called Orchid Island, numbered 4,684 in January 2020.

nations.name: Mizo
nations.lands: Mizoram, northeast India

facts.text: Mizoram became a full state of India on 20 February 1987; its Legislative Assembly first met on 10 May 1972.
Historically, every Mizo village had its own chief, who was assisted by a council of elders.

nations.name: Chakma
nations.lands: Chittagong Hill Tracts of Bangladesh, and parts of northeast India

facts.text: Hill Tracts peoples are sometimes called Jumma, after jum, their traditional method of shifting cultivation.
The Chakma make up more than half of the Indigenous population of Bangladesh's Chittagong Hill Tracts.

nations.name: Naga
nations.lands: Nagaland, Manipur and Arunachal Pradesh in India, and neighbouring Myanmar

facts.text: Nagaland's state portal lists 17 major tribes living in the state, each with its own language and festivals.

source.title: People and Culture
source.publisher: Nagaland State Portal, Government of Nagaland

facts.text: Each December the Government of Nagaland hosts the Hornbill Festival near Kohima, where all the state's tribes share their cultures.

nations.name: Newa
nations.lands: Swanigah, the Kathmandu Valley (Kathmandu, Lalitpur and Bhaktapur), and towns across Nepal

facts.text: In 2021 Nepal's Language Commission recommended Nepal Bhasa, alongside Tamang, as an official language of Bagmati Province.

source.title: Language Commission recommends province-wise official languages before government

facts.text: Nepal Bhasa, the Newa language, has its own scripts, Ranjana and Prachalit, along with its own grammar, dictionaries and literature.

source.title: नेवार (Newar)
source.publisher: National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities, Nepal

nations.name: Garo
nations.lands: Garo Hills of Meghalaya, India, and north-central Bangladesh

facts.text: The Garo Hills Autonomous District Council, set up in 1952 under India's Sixth Schedule, is based in Tura and covers five districts.
The Meghalaya government lists Garo among the state's languages, alongside Khasi, Pnar and English.

nations.name: Orang Asli
nations.lands: Peninsular Malaysia

facts.text: Orang Asli, a Malay collective term meaning original or first peoples, covers 18 officially listed groups of Peninsular Malaysia.
Some Temuan, Jakun and Semai families now run their own rubber, oil palm or cocoa farms.

nations.name: Atayal
nations.lands: Mountain areas of northern and central Taiwan, across New Taipei, Taoyuan, Hsinchu, Miaoli, Taichung, Nantou and Yilan

facts.text: In the Atayal language, the word Atayal means people, real people, or kinspeople.
The Atayal live across the mountains of northern and central Taiwan, the widest spread of any Indigenous people on the island.

nations.name: Iban
nations.lands: Sarawak, Malaysia, with communities in West Kalimantan, Indonesia, and Brunei

facts.text: Between 1948 and 1963 the Iban language served as the common language between Sarawak's communities.

source.title: Indigenous peoples and ethnic minorities in Sarawak

facts.text: In 2011 the Tun Jugah Foundation published Bup Sereba Reti Jaku Iban, described as the first monolingual Iban dictionary.

nations.name: Mru
nations.lands: Bandarban district in the Chittagong Hill Tracts of Bangladesh, and nearby areas of Myanmar

facts.text: The Mru alphabet, invented in the 1980s and unrelated to any other script, is encoded in the Unicode Standard with its own digits.

source.title: Chapter 13, South and Central Asia-II (The Unicode Standard, Version 18.0)

facts.text: School textbooks up to class three have been published in the Mru language and alphabet.

nations.name: Kavalan
nations.lands: Yilan and the Hualien and Taitung coasts, Taiwan

facts.text: After a name rectification movement, the Kavalan were officially recognized as one of Taiwan's Indigenous peoples in 2002.
The Kavalan population was about 1,492 in January 2020.

nations.name: Kadazandusun
nations.lands: Sabah, Malaysia

facts.text: The Kadazan Dusun Cultural Association, founded in 1966, represents 48 Indigenous ethnic communities of Sabah.
KDCA works on preserving, standardizing and developing the Kadazandusun language with its many dialects.

nations.name: Rapa Nui
nations.lands: Rapa Nui (Easter Island), in the south-eastern Pacific, Chile

facts.text: Tapati Rapa Nui, the island's main cultural festival, filled two weeks of February 2026 with ancestral competitions, arts and celebrations of Rapa Nui identity, language and traditions.

source.title: Ministra de las Culturas participa en inauguración de la Tapati Rapanui y desarrolla agenda de trabajo en la isla
source.publisher: Ministerio de las Culturas, las Artes y el Patrimonio (Chile)

facts.text: In 2017, 642 votes were cast in a formal consultation with the Rapa Nui people on a marine protected area for their island, and yes won all three questions.

source.title: Informe del Proceso de Consulta al pueblo Rapa Nui sobre creación, administración y regulación de usos de un Área Marina Costera Protegida de Múltiples Usos para Rapa Nui
source.publisher: Ministerio del Medio Ambiente, Gobierno de Chile

nations.name: Aṉangu
nations.lands: Central Australia, including Uluṟu-Kata Tjuṯa in the Northern Territory and the APY Lands of South Australia

facts.text: The park's board of management has 12 people, including eight Aboriginal members nominated by Traditional Owners.

source.title: Joint management | Uluṟu-Kata Tjuṯa National Park | Parks Australia

facts.text: Uluṟu-Kata Tjuṯa National Park was handed back to its Aṉangu Traditional Owners in 1985 and is jointly managed today.

source.title: Joint management | Uluṟu-Kata Tjuṯa National Park | Parks Australia

nations.name: Cook Islands Māori
nations.lands: the Cook Islands, including Rarotonga and the Southern and Northern Group islands

facts.text: Te Maeva Nui, held every early August, marks Cook Islands self-governance on 4 August and gathers communities from every island for song, dance, drumming and chant.
A 2003 law declared Cook Islands Māori an official language of the Cook Islands, alongside English, and set up a Māori language commission.

source.title: Te Reo Maori Act 2003 (Cook Islands)
source.publisher: Université Laval, CEFAN: L'aménagement linguistique dans le monde

nations.name: Yawuru
nations.lands: Broome (Rubibi) and the surrounding lands and seas, Kimberley, Western Australia, Australia

facts.text: Up to 1,500 children in Broome primary schools take part in Yawuru language programs.
In 2006 the Federal Court recognised Yawuru people as native title holders of about 530,000 hectares of country in and around Broome.

nations.name: Gunditjmara
nations.lands: South-west Victoria, including Budj Bim and Tae Rak (Lake Condah), Australia

facts.text: Gunditj Mirring Traditional Owners Aboriginal Corporation was set up in 2005 to continue Gunditjmara connection to country, including native title work.

source.title: Gunditj Mirring Traditional Owners Aboriginal Corporation | GMTOAC | 248 Condah Estate Road, Heywood VIC, Australia
source.publisher: Gunditj Mirring Traditional Owners Aboriginal Corporation

facts.text: All of the Budj Bim Cultural Landscape is Aboriginal owned or managed.

source.title: World heritage conservation of Budj Bim

nations.name: Te Arawa
nations.lands: Rotorua and the Rotorua lakes district, Bay of Plenty, Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: Rotorua was declared New Zealand's first bilingual district in 2017, and the council has since worked with Te Tatau o Te Arawa on changes like bilingual road signs.
The Te Arawa Lakes settlement, signed in 2004, provided for title to 13 lakebeds to be returned to Te Arawa, a large confederation of iwi and hapū.

source.title: Te Arawa Lakes
source.publisher: Te Kāhui Whakatau (Treaty Settlements), New Zealand Government

nations.name: Yapese
nations.lands: the main islands of Yap (Yap, Gagil, Tomil and Rumung) in Yap State, Federated States of Micronesia

facts.text: Yap's state constitution creates the Council of Pilung and the Council of Tamol, councils of traditional leaders whose work concerns tradition and custom.

source.title: Yap State Code, Title 5: Traditional Leaders and Traditions
source.publisher: Legal Information System of the Federated States of Micronesia

facts.text: Under Yap State law the two councils advise the Governor and Legislature and work to promote and preserve the traditions and customs of the people.

source.title: Yap State Code, Title 5: Traditional Leaders and Traditions
source.publisher: Legal Information System of the Federated States of Micronesia

nations.name: Tuvaluans
nations.lands: the nine islands of Tuvalu in the central Pacific, including Funafuti

facts.text: Each island in Tuvalu has a falekaupule, a traditional assembly of elders also called te sina o fenua, the grey-hairs of the land.

source.title: The Local Government System in Tuvalu

facts.text: Tuvaluan has eight dialects from eight of the islands, and the name Tuvalu joins tu, to stand, with valu, eight.

source.title: Tuvalu language activity book
source.publisher: Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa

nations.name: Arrernte
nations.lands: Alice Springs and surrounding lands in Central Australia, Northern Territory, Australia

facts.text: Lhere Artepe Aboriginal Corporation, their native title body, looks after five Indigenous Land Use Agreements plus a land release agreement.

source.title: About Us | Lhere Artepe Aboriginal Corporation

facts.text: Arrernte people from three estate groups, Antulye, Irlpme and Mparntwe, are the traditional owners of Alice Springs and its surrounding land.

source.title: About Us | Lhere Artepe Aboriginal Corporation

nations.name: Tongans
nations.lands: the Kingdom of Tonga in the South Pacific, including Tongatapu, Vava'u, Ha'apai, 'Eua and the Niuas

facts.text: Tonga's 2021 census counted 100,179 people in the kingdom, a young population with a median age of 19 for males and 22 for females.
Lakalaka, often called Tonga's national dance, joins choreography, oratory and sung polyphony, and is performed at coronations and constitution anniversaries.

source.title: Lakalaka, dances and sung speeches of Tonga

nations.name: Tiwi
nations.lands: The Tiwi Islands (Bathurst and Melville Islands), about 80 km north of Darwin in the Arafura Sea, Northern Territory, Australia

facts.text: There are eight landowning groups on the Tiwi Islands, and Tiwi people have an unbroken history of occupying and owning their islands.
The Tiwi Islands, about 80 km north of Darwin, are home to just over 3,000 people, more than 90 percent of them Tiwi.

nations.name: Gamilaraay
nations.lands: North-central New South Wales into southern Queensland, Australia

facts.text: The Australian National University teaches Gamilaraay as a heritage language that its custodians are actively reviving.

source.title: Gamilaraay - Introduction to an Australian Indigenous Language

facts.text: Student work in the ANU Gamilaraay course feeds into materials for Gamilaraay and Yuwaalaraay language revival, taught with a free textbook called Wiidhaa.

source.title: Gamilaraay - Introduction to an Australian Indigenous Language

nations.name: Ngāti Porou
nations.lands: Te Tairāwhiti, the East Coast of the North Island, from Pōtikirua to Te Toka-a-Taiau, Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: Ngāti Porou's tribal area runs down Te Tairāwhiti, between Pōtikirua (Lottin Point) in the north and Te Toka-a-Taiau in the south.
The Ngāti Porou pepeha names Hikurangi as their mountain and Waiapu as their river.

nations.name: ni-Vanuatu
nations.lands: the islands of the Republic of Vanuatu in the south-west Pacific, including Malakula and the central and northern islands

facts.text: Vanuatu Cultural Centre fieldworkers, or filwokas, are volunteers nominated by their communities across the islands to promote, protect and preserve kastom.

source.title: Grassroots Badly Burnt: the loss of ni-Vanuatu archaeologists whose careers spanned 50 years

facts.text: In 1998 Na'hai speakers of south Malakula opened the Na'hai Kaljaral Senta, the first language-based cultural centre in Vanuatu.

source.title: Kastom as Development: Opening the Na'hai Kaljaral Senta

nations.name: Meriam
nations.lands: Mer (Murray Island) and nearby islands in the eastern Torres Strait, Queensland, Australia

facts.text: Meriam Mir is the traditional language of Mer, an island in the far east of the Torres Strait from which the Great Barrier Reef can be seen.

source.title: Murray Island - Mer Eruer Uteb
source.publisher: Tagai State College (Queensland Department of Education)

nations.name: Rotumans
nations.lands: the island of Rotuma and its islets, about 500 km north of Fiji's main islands, and communities across Fiji

facts.text: Rotuma is divided into seven districts, each led by a district chief, the gagaj 'es itu'u, with village groups called ho'aga under their own chiefs.

source.title: Hierarchy (Kato'aga: Rotuman Ceremonies)
source.publisher: The Rotuma Website, University of Hawai'i

facts.text: Rotumans are a distinct people with their own language, Fäeag Rotuạm, which New Zealand celebrates each year in Rotuman Language Week.

source.title: Gasav Ne Fäeag Rotuạm Ta: Rotuman Language Week

nations.name: Kanak
nations.lands: New Caledonia, including Grande Terre and the Loyalty Islands

facts.text: Since 2016 every pupil in New Caledonia must be taught the fundamentals of Kanak culture, and every school must offer teaching in Kanak languages.

source.title: Organisation coutumière kanak
source.publisher: Institut de la statistique et des études économiques Nouvelle-Calédonie (ISEE)

facts.text: Kanak society is organised by custom: clans join into tribes within customary districts, which are grouped into eight customary areas.

source.title: Organisation coutumière kanak
source.publisher: Institut de la statistique et des études économiques Nouvelle-Calédonie (ISEE)

nations.name: Ngāi Tūhoe
nations.lands: Te Urewera, in the eastern North Island, Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: A Treaty settlement signed in 2013 provided for Te Urewera, the Tūhoe homeland, to have its own law and a separate legal identity, governed by Tūhoe and Crown nominees.

source.title: Ngāi Tūhoe
source.publisher: Te Kāhui Whakatau (Treaty Settlements), New Zealand Government

facts.text: Tūhoe had about 9,300 registered members at the time of their 2013 Treaty settlement.

source.title: Ngāi Tūhoe
source.publisher: Te Kāhui Whakatau (Treaty Settlements), New Zealand Government

nations.name: Tokelauans
nations.lands: the three atolls of Tokelau, Atafu, Nukunonu and Fakaofo, in the South Pacific

facts.text: In Tokelau the Taupulega, the village councils of elders, remain the ultimate source of authority, and they grant the General Fono its powers.
The role of Ulu-o-Tokelau, head of the national government, rotates each year among the elected leaders of Tokelau's three atolls.

nations.name: I-Kiribati
nations.lands: the Republic of Kiribati in the central Pacific, across the Gilbert, Phoenix and Line Islands

facts.text: In Kiribati the mwaneaba, the traditional meeting house, is where village decisions are made by the unimwane, the senior men, whose seating shows their standing.

source.title: Te Mwaneaba ni Kiribati: The Traditional Meeting House of Kiribati
source.publisher: Shima: The International Journal of Research into Island Cultures

facts.text: In 2010 the Phoenix Islands Protected Area, about 408,250 square kilometres of ocean and islands, became the first World Heritage site in Kiribati.

nations.name: Wiradjuri
nations.lands: Central New South Wales, the country of the Wambool (Macquarie), Kalari (Lachlan) and Murrumbidjeri (Murrumbidgee) rivers, Australia

facts.text: A Charles Sturt University course shaped by Wiradjuri Elders works to build a living community of Wiradjuri speakers; it won a 2019 MacJannet Prize.

source.title: The Graduate Certificate in Wiradjuri Language Culture and Heritage, Charles Sturt University (Australia)
source.publisher: Talloires Network of Engaged Universities (Tufts University)

facts.text: Wiradjuri country covers a large part of New South Wales, reaching out from the Great Dividing Range.

nations.name: Papuan peoples
nations.lands: The Papua region of Indonesia, the western half of the island of New Guinea

facts.text: Men and women in Papua use the noken to carry garden produce, and it may also be worn at festivities or given as a peace offering.

source.title: Noken multifunctional knotted or woven bag, handcraft of the people of Papua

facts.text: The noken, a bag that communities in Papua knot or weave by hand from wood fibre or leaves, was inscribed on a UNESCO list for urgent safeguarding in 2012.

source.title: Noken multifunctional knotted or woven bag, handcraft of the people of Papua

nations.name: Mā'ohi
nations.lands: French Polynesia, including Tahiti and the other islands of its five archipelagos

facts.text: A new website interface announced in 2017 by the Tahitian Academy, Fare Vāna'a, adds French to Tahitian search to its Tahitian to French dictionary.

source.title: Evolution du site internet du Fare Vāna’a & application
source.publisher: Service public de la Polynésie française (DGEN)

facts.text: UNESCO honours mā'ohi skill in sailing outrigger canoes across long stretches of ocean, navigating by observing natural phenomena.

nations.name: Benet
nations.lands: the slopes of Mount Elgon in eastern Uganda, in Kween, Kapchorwa and Bukwo districts

facts.text: In May 2023 Uganda's Office of the Prime Minister directed the wildlife authority (UWA) to stop evictions of Benet communities.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, Uganda chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: In 2005 Uganda's High Court recognized the Benet as the historical, indigenous inhabitants of Mount Elgon, a landmark land-rights ruling.

source.title: Momentous Ruling Recognizes Land Rights of Indigenous Community

nations.name: Bagyeli
nations.lands: the forests of southern Cameroon, around Akom II, Bipindi, Kribi and Lolodorf

facts.text: In late 2018 Bagyeli communities filed three Community Forest applications with Cameroon's forestry ministry, after mapping their own forest use.

source.title: Secure land tenure: The legal battles of the Bagyeli

facts.text: Bagyeli and Bakola communities live across about 12,000 km2 of southern Cameroon, especially around Akom II, Bipindi, Kribi and Lolodorf.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, Cameroon chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Ovahimba
nations.lands: Kunene Region of north-western Namibia and south-western Angola

facts.text: Ovahimba speak a Herero language and keep semi-nomadic herding homelands that reach from north-western Namibia into south-western Angola.
Ovahimba are mainly herders whose homes lie in the dry mountains and plains of north-west Namibia's Kunene Region.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Namibia
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Oromo
nations.lands: Oromia and other regions of Ethiopia, and northern Kenya

facts.text: Knowledge of the Gada system is passed on to Oromo children today, at home and at school.

source.title: Gada system, an indigenous democratic socio-political system of the Oromo

facts.text: UNESCO lists the Gada system as an indigenous democratic socio-political system of the Oromo, inscribed on its heritage list in 2016.

source.title: Gada system, an indigenous democratic socio-political system of the Oromo

nations.name: Ishelhiyen
nations.lands: the Souss valley, the Anti-Atlas and the western High Atlas of south-western Morocco

facts.text: In the Souss-Massa region, 63.2% of residents use Tachelhit, the language of the Ishelhin, according to Morocco's 2024 census.

source.title: RGPH 2024: Caractéristiques démographiques et socioéconomiques de la population, Région Souss-Massa
source.publisher: Haut-Commissariat au Plan (HCP), Direction Régionale de Souss Massa

facts.text: Tachelhit, the language of the Ishelhin of southern Morocco, is one of three Amazigh languages taught at Inalco in Paris.

source.title: Kabyle (Berber)
source.publisher: Inalco (Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales)

nations.name: Hadzabe
nations.lands: the hills and valleys around Lake Eyasi in northern Tanzania

facts.text: Hadzabe communities are calling for community-led tourism that ensures transparency, dignity and a fair share of the benefits.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Tanzania
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: Hadza people speak Hadzane, a language isolate, which means it is not related to any other known language.

nations.name: Nama
nations.lands: southern Namibia and the Richtersveld and Namaqualand areas of South Africa's Northern Cape, with smaller communities in Botswana

facts.text: In 2003 South Africa's Constitutional Court recognized the Richtersveld Nama community's communal Indigenous right to its land and the resources in it.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: South Africa
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: In South Africa's Richtersveld, Nama families still build portable rush-mat houses called haru oms and move herds between seasonal grazing grounds.

nations.name: Mbororo
nations.lands: Cameroon, Chad, Nigeria, the Central African Republic and Niger, often along borderland grazing routes

facts.text: Hindou Oumarou Ibrahim, a Mbororo woman from Chad who founded the group AFPAT, chaired the UN Permanent Forum on Indigenous Issues for its 2024 session.

source.title: Previous Chairpersons of the Permanent Forum
source.publisher: United Nations, Department of Economic and Social Affairs (UNPFII)

facts.text: Mbororo pastoralists in Cameroon are estimated at over one million people, living mainly near the borders with Nigeria, Chad and the Central African Republic.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Cameroon
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Naro
nations.lands: Ghanzi District in western Botswana, and eastern Namibia

facts.text: In 2025 Botswana's government started radio programs in a number of Indigenous languages, Naro among them.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Botswana
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: Botswana chose Naro, the main San language of Ghanzi District, as one of the mother-tongue languages for primary school teaching from 2022.

source.title: Forty years of fighting for literacy The case of Naro Bible translators

nations.name: Tshwa
nations.lands: Tsholotsho and Bulilimamangwe districts of western Zimbabwe

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, Zimbabwe chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)

nations.name: Batwa
nations.lands: south-western Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi and the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo

source.title: The Indigenous World 2023: Burundi
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

source.title: MRG welcomes Uganda court verdict on Batwa compensation

nations.name: Samburu
nations.lands: Samburu County and nearby rangelands of north-central Kenya

source.title: Home | Reteti Elephant Sanctuary in Kenya

source.title: Empowering women means taking a stand for environmental rights

nations.name: Khoikhoi
nations.lands: South Africa, especially the Western, Northern and Eastern Cape, including Nama, Griqua and Korana communities

facts.text: Rooibos benefit money now helps fund local schools, water pumps, student fees and an organic rooibos nursery in Cederberg communities such as Wupperthal.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: South Africa
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

source.title: Kora: A Lost Khoisan Language of the early Cape and the Gariep, Introduction (Menán du Plessis)

nations.name: ǂKhomani
nations.lands: the southern Kalahari in South Africa's Northern Cape, including the Kalahari Gemsbok National Park near the borders with Botswana and Namibia

facts.text: ǂKhomani people have won back cultural rights in South Africa's Kalahari Gemsbok National Park, such as using its resources and hunting in traditional ways across much of it.
The ǂKhomani are actively reclaiming their knowledge and traditions. Their Kalahari homeland became a UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape in 2017.

nations.name: Ju|'hoansi
nations.lands: Nyae Nyae and the Tsumkwe area of north-eastern Namibia, and neighbouring north-western Botswana

facts.text: When Ju|'hoansi formed their farmers' cooperative, they began with open consensus meetings, then elected two representatives per community, at least one of them a woman.

source.title: Controlling Their Destiny: Ju|'hoansi of Nyae Nyae

facts.text: Ju|'hoansi is the one San language Namibia has approved for teaching in schools, but a 2025 review of 14 schools found it is seldom used in class.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Namibia
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Mbuti
nations.lands: the Ituri forest of north-eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo

facts.text: A 2022 national law in the DR Congo, in force since February 2023, recognizes the rights of Indigenous peoples, including the Mbuti, to their lands, territories and resources.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024: Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: UNESCO calls for ensuring the involvement of the Indigenous Mbuti and Efe peoples in the management of the Okapi Wildlife Reserve.

nations.name: Karimojong
nations.lands: the Karamoja drylands of north-eastern Uganda

facts.text: The Karimojong, whose economy has long rested on livestock, live mainly in the drylands of north-eastern Uganda, about 1.09 million people in a 2018 estimate.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, Uganda chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: Cultural Heritage Clubs in five secondary schools in Napak and Moroto treat heritage as central to Karimojong history and identity.

source.title: Karamoja Cultural Heritage Education Programme
source.publisher: Kara-Tunga (partner of Cross Cultural Foundation Uganda)

nations.name: !Xun
nations.lands: north-eastern Namibia and southern Angola, and Platfontein near Kimberley in South Africa

facts.text: In South Africa, !Xun and Khwe communities live mainly at Platfontein, near Kimberley.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, South Africa chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: XK FM, a public station first on air in 2000, now broadcasts from Platfontein about 15 hours a day in the !Xun and Khwe languages.

source.title: MEDIA STATEMENT | SABC CELEBRATES THE HISTORY AND CULTURE OF THE !XU AND KHWE

nations.name: Maasai
nations.lands: southern Kenya and northern Tanzania, on both sides of the border

facts.text: In 2025 Tanzania's Simanjiro district paused carbon project signings for 30 days to respond to community concerns, which IWGIA read as a sign that communities are starting to be heard.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Tanzania
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: Maasai people speak Maa, a Nilotic language related to Dinka, Kalenjin and Nuer.

nations.name: Korana
nations.lands: Kimberley and the Free State province, South Africa

facts.text: Korana communities live mainly in Kimberley and in the Free State province.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, South Africa chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: In their own !Ora language, the Korana's name for themselves is !Orakua or !Orana.

source.title: Kora: A Lost Khoisan Language of the early Cape and the Gariep, Introduction (Menán du Plessis)

nations.name: Afar
nations.lands: the Afar region of north-eastern Ethiopia, the Dankalia coast of Eritrea, and Djibouti

facts.text: In 2008 Afar pastoralists set up the Afar Pastoralist Council so they could raise their voices at regional, national and international level.

source.title: Afar Pastoralist Council holds Inaugural General Meeting

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, Eritrea chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Delaware Nation
nations.lands: Anadarko, Oklahoma, United States; Lenape homelands on the Eastern Seaboard

facts.text: Delaware Nation is a federally recognized tribe based in Anadarko, Oklahoma.

source.title: Delaware Nation Re-Established THPO Status with the National Park Services and US Department of Interior

nations.name: Wampanoag Tribe of Gay Head (Aquinnah)
nations.lands: Aquinnah, on the western end of Martha's Vineyard (Noepe), Massachusetts, United States

facts.text: The Aquinnah Wampanoag care for 477 acres of their ancestral lands on Martha's Vineyard.
In 1998 the town of Gay Head returned to its former Wampanoag name, Aquinnah.

nations.name: Tuscarora Nation
nations.lands: Tuscarora Nation territory near Lewiston, western New York, United States; earlier homelands in what is now North Carolina

facts.text: The Tuscarora Language Program works with one clear mission: to revive a community of Tuscarora speakers.
The Tuscarora Environment Program works as part of the Haudenosaunee Environmental Task Force, established in 1992 by the Grand Council.

nations.name: Mashpee Wampanoag Tribe
nations.lands: Mashpee on Cape Cod, Massachusetts, United States; Wampanoag homelands across present-day Massachusetts and eastern Rhode Island

facts.text: The Mashpee Wampanoag were re-acknowledged as a federally recognized tribe in 2007.

source.title: Mashpee Wampanoag Tribe | People of the First Light

facts.text: Children at Mukayuhsak Weekuw, the Mashpee Wampanoag language nest, could be the first in centuries to grow up proficient in Wôpanâak.

nations.name: Chickahominy Indian Tribe
nations.lands: the Chickahominy River area and Chickahominy Ridge in Virginia, as described in the Tribe's history

facts.text: The Chickahominy Indian Tribe's history describes permanent villages along the Virginia river that still bears its name.
The Tribe dates the establishment of Samaria Indian Baptist Church, a community institution, to 1901.

nations.name: United Keetoowah Band of Cherokee Indians in Oklahoma
nations.lands: Tahlequah, Oklahoma, United States

facts.text: The UKB Tribal Council is made up of four officers and nine district representatives, governing from Tahlequah, Oklahoma.

source.title: United Keetoowah Band | Home | Tahlequah, OK
source.publisher: United Keetoowah Band of Cherokee Indians in Oklahoma

facts.text: The United Keetoowah Band numbers more than 14,000 tribal members today.

source.title: About Us | United Keetoowah Band | Tahlequah
source.publisher: United Keetoowah Band of Cherokee Indians in Oklahoma

nations.name: Monacan Indian Nation
nations.lands: Bear Mountain in Amherst County, Virginia; the Nation describes ancestral homelands extending through Virginia and parts of West Virginia and North Carolina

facts.text: The Nation says its Priority Climate Action Plan includes a greenhouse gas inventory to guide conservation and emissions-reduction work.
The Nation describes its citizens as descendants of Virginia and North Carolina Eastern Siouan cultural and linguistic groups.

nations.name: Nansemond Indian Nation
nations.lands: the Nansemond River area of southeastern Virginia; the Nation describes traditional settlements extending into northeastern North Carolina

facts.text: The Nation's published Environmental Program describes oyster restoration, invasive plant removal and native plant restoration.
The Nation's history dates formal organization with elected officers to 1984.

nations.name: Muscogee Nation
nations.lands: Okmulgee and the Muscogee reservation in eastern Oklahoma, United States; original homelands in present-day Georgia and Alabama

facts.text: Seated in Okmulgee, Oklahoma, the Muscogee (Creek) Nation is self-governed and organized by its Constitution into three branches of government.
The Mvskoke Language Program offers classes and learning resources so Mvskoke people can keep their language, culture and sovereignty strong.

nations.name: Chickahominy Indian Tribe - Eastern Division
nations.lands: New Kent County, Virginia; the Tribe describes roots in Virginia before English colonization

facts.text: In its food-sovereignty account, CIT-ED says a 2022 EPA grant supported a community compost and gardening program.
The Tribe's timeline records a certificate of incorporation for the Chickahominy Indians Eastern Division in 1925.

nations.name: Narragansett Indian Tribe
nations.lands: Rhode Island, United States

facts.text: The Narragansett Indian Tribe received federal recognition and acknowledgement on April 11, 1983.
A land claim brought by the Tribe ended in a 1978 out-of-court settlement of about 1,800 acres.

nations.name: Passamaquoddy (Peskotomuhkati)
nations.lands: Sipayik (Pleasant Point) and Motahkomikuk (Indian Township) in Maine, United States, and a community in New Brunswick, Canada

facts.text: Over 3,000 Passamaquoddy citizens belong to three self-governing communities, two in Maine and one in New Brunswick, linked by political, cultural and kinship ties.
The Maliseet-Passamaquoddy Dictionary has more than 19,000 entries, and many older tribal members still speak the language fluently.

nations.name: MOWA Band of Choctaw Indians
nations.lands: Mobile and Washington Counties in southwestern Alabama, near the Mobile and Tombigbee Rivers

facts.text: The Tribe's introduction places its communities in Mobile and Washington Counties in southwestern Alabama.
Its history dates an effort to obtain federal aid for Alabama Choctaw schools to 1934.

source.title: Social Barriers - MOWA Band of Choctaw Indians

nations.name: Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians
nations.lands: Choctaw communities in east-central Mississippi, United States

facts.text: In 1945 the Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians ratified a Constitution that authorized the Tribe's separation from the state of Mississippi.

source.title: About Us - Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians

facts.text: The Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians has more than 11,000 tribal members.

source.title: Home Page - Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians

nations.name: Choctaw Nation of Oklahoma
nations.lands: Durant and a reservation of eight whole and five partial counties in southeastern Oklahoma, United States; original homelands in present-day Mississippi

facts.text: Chahta Anumpa Aiikhvna, the School of Choctaw Language, offers classes for every skill level plus a Speak Choctaw app.
The Choctaw Nation reservation covers 10,864 square miles in southeastern Oklahoma, taking in eight whole counties and parts of five more.

nations.name: Cheroenhaka (Nottoway) Indian Tribe
nations.lands: Southampton County, Virginia, United States

facts.text: Cheroenhaka (Nottoway) Indian Tribe is based in Southampton County, Virginia.
The Tribe's language page publishes a vocabulary drawn from materials dating to March 4, 1820.

nations.name: Cayuga Nation
nations.lands: Around Cayuga Lake in the Finger Lakes region of New York, United States

facts.text: After more than 200 years away, Cayuga Nation citizens once again live on their ancestral homeland in New York's Finger Lakes region.
Every citizen of the Cayuga Nation belongs to one of the Nation's five clans.

nations.name: Pamunkey Indian Tribe
nations.lands: Pamunkey Reservation on the Pamunkey River, King William County, Virginia, United States

facts.text: The U.S. Department of the Interior acknowledged the Pamunkey Indian Tribe as federally recognized, effective January 28, 2016.
The Pamunkey reservation sits on the northern bank of the Pamunkey River in King William County, Virginia.

nations.name: Cherokee Tribe of Northeast Alabama
nations.lands: Northeast Alabama; its own introduction traces its roots to the lower Cherokee towns.

facts.text: Its government page describes a Tribal Council with one representative for each district.
Its Learning Tools page presents a syllabary song and a public word-learning list.

nations.name: Upper Mattaponi Tribe
nations.lands: King William County, Virginia; the Tribe describes its community base as within the traditional lands of Tsenacomacah

facts.text: The Tribe's school history says King William County returned Sharon Indian School to the Tribe in 1987.

source.title: Sharon Indian School Foundation - Upper Mattaponi Tribe

facts.text: The Tribe's history says the Adamstown band became officially known as the Upper Mattaponi Tribe in 1921.

nations.name: Northern Cheyenne Tribe
nations.lands: Northern Cheyenne Reservation, southeastern Montana, United States; headquarters in Lame Deer

facts.text: Lame Deer, Montana, is home to the Northern Cheyenne tribal government headquarters, and the Tribal Council is elected by district.

source.title: Northern Cheyenne Tribe
source.publisher: Montana Governor's Office of Indian Affairs

facts.text: About 99 percent of the Northern Cheyenne Reservation, roughly 444,000 acres in southeastern Montana, is owned by the tribe.

source.title: Northern Cheyenne Tribe
source.publisher: Montana Governor's Office of Indian Affairs

nations.name: Comanche Nation
nations.lands: Southwest Oklahoma, United States; headquarters north of Lawton

facts.text: The Comanche Nation's main governing body is its Tribal Council, made up of every enrolled member over age 18.
The Comanche Nation language program works to revitalize and reclaim the Comanche language, including through online learning.

pronounce.text: Nʉmʉnʉʉ, the Comanche name for the people: NUH-MUH-NUH
pronounce.publisher: Comanche Nation, on its own site

nations.name: Apsáalooke Nation
nations.lands: Crow Indian Reservation, south-central Montana, United States; headquarters at Crow Agency

source.title: Official Site of the Crow Tribe Executive Branch - Home

facts.text: Montana's state tribal directory reports that most Apsáalooke people speak Crow as their first language.

source.title: Crow Nation
source.publisher: Montana Governor's Office of Indian Affairs

nations.name: Spirit Lake Nation
nations.lands: Northeastern North Dakota, mainly Benson County, United States; headquarters at Fort Totten

facts.text: Cankdeska Cikana Community College, the tribal college at Spirit Lake, offers 12 associate degree and certificate programs.

source.title: Spirit Lake Nation | Indian Affairs Commission, North Dakota

source.title: Spirit Lake Nation | Indian Affairs Commission, North Dakota

nations.name: Fort Sill Apache Tribe
nations.lands: Apache and Fletcher, Oklahoma; reservation land in New Mexico, United States

facts.text: The Fort Sill Apache Tribe comprises descendants of Chiricahua and Warm Springs Apaches displaced from the Southwest and northern Mexico.
The General Council, made up of adult tribal members, elects the Business Committee and approves the tribal operations budget.

nations.name: Oneida Nation
also: Oneida Tribe of Indians of Wisconsin
nations.lands: Oneida Reservation, Brown and Outagamie counties, northeast Wisconsin, United States

facts.text: The Oneida Nation is governed by an elected Business Committee of nine members, which makes decisions by majority rule.

source.title: Oneida Nation | Department of Public Instruction

facts.text: The Oneida Reservation lies in Brown and Outagamie counties in northeast Wisconsin.

source.title: Oneida Nation | Department of Public Instruction

nations.name: Mandan, Hidatsa, and Arikara Nation
nations.lands: Fort Berthold Indian Reservation, central North Dakota, United States

facts.text: The MHA Nation is governed by a Chairman and six Segment Representatives, one each for White Shield, Parshall, New Town, Four Bears, Mandaree and Twin Buttes.

source.title: MHA Nation | Mandan, Hidatsa, and Arikara Nation

facts.text: The nation greets visitors in all three of its languages. In Mandan, Ráátinitak shí’sh means it is good that you all arrived.

source.title: MHA Nation | Mandan, Hidatsa, and Arikara Nation

nations.name: Northern Arapaho Tribe
nations.lands: Wind River Reservation, Wyoming, United States, shared with the Eastern Shoshone

facts.text: The Northern Arapaho and the Eastern Shoshone share a 2.2 million acre reservation in Wyoming, between the Wind River Range and the Owl Creek Mountains.
The Arapaho Flag was created in 1936 to honor and remember Arapaho war veterans.

nations.name: Sac and Fox Nation
nations.lands: Central Oklahoma, United States; headquarters in Stroud

facts.text: The Sac and Fox Nation supports learning Sauk through an interactive language website and a concise Sauk dictionary.
The Sac and Fox Nation was the first tribe to take on self-governance within the Indian Health Service.

nations.name: Forest County Potawatomi
nations.lands: Forest County, northern Wisconsin, United States

facts.text: The Forest County Potawatomi Language and Culture Department works to keep the Bodwéwadmi language and traditions alive, with classes during the school year.
The Forest County Potawatomi Cultural Center, Library and Museum provides an important link to the community's past.

nations.name: Red Lake Nation
also: Red Lake Band of Chippewa Indians
nations.lands: Red Lake Reservation, northern Minnesota, United States

facts.text: The Red Lake tribal government holds full sovereignty over its reservation, subject only to the federal government.

source.title: Red Lake Nation - Home of the Red Lake Band of Chippewa Indians

facts.text: English is a second language for many Red Lake members who are middle-aged and older, including some on the Tribal Council, and many others speak or understand Ojibwe.

nations.name: Kiowa Tribe
nations.lands: Southwestern Oklahoma, United States

facts.text: The Kiowa Tribe commits to protecting its sovereignty and to preserving and advocating for Kiowa culture and language.

source.title: Kiowa Tribe - Tribe, Native American, Native, Tribe

facts.text: The Kiowa Language Department runs a credentialed teacher training program to prepare new Kiowa language teachers.

pronounce.publisher: Kiowa Tribe, on its own site

nations.name: Blackfeet Nation
nations.lands: Blackfeet Reservation, northwestern Montana, bordering Canada and Glacier National Park, United States

facts.text: The Blackfeet Reservation covers about one and a half million acres, bordered by Canada to the north and Glacier National Park to the west.

source.title: Blackfeet Nation
source.publisher: Montana Governor's Office of Indian Affairs

facts.text: The Blackfeet Nation describes itself as a nation of 17,321 members.

nations.name: Oglala Sioux Tribe
nations.lands: Pine Ridge Reservation, southwestern South Dakota, United States

source.publisher: U.S. Department of the Interior, Bureau of Indian Affairs

nations.name: Omaha Tribe of Nebraska
nations.lands: Omaha Reservation, Nebraska, United States; tribal offices in Macy

facts.text: The Omaha Tribe of Nebraska holds a trust land base of 27,828 acres, according to the Bureau of Indian Affairs.

source.title: Winnebago Agency | Indian Affairs
source.publisher: U.S. Department of the Interior, Bureau of Indian Affairs

facts.text: The Bureau of Indian Affairs estimates enrollment in the Omaha Tribe of Nebraska at 5,427 members.

source.publisher: U.S. Department of the Interior, Bureau of Indian Affairs

nations.name: Mille Lacs Band of Ojibwe
nations.lands: Three districts in East Central Minnesota, United States

facts.text: The Mille Lacs Band governs itself through a three-branch government that divides power among executive, legislative and judicial branches.

source.title: Welcome | Mille Lacs Band of Ojibwe

facts.text: The Mille Lacs Band is a self-governing nation of nearly 4,800 enrolled members, with homelands in three districts of East Central Minnesota.

source.title: Welcome | Mille Lacs Band of Ojibwe

nations.name: Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa Indians
nations.lands: Rolette County, North Dakota, near the Canadian border, United States

facts.text: Members of the Turtle Mountain Band speak English, Ojibwe and Michif, a language that blends French, Ojibwe and Cree.

source.title: Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa | Indian Affairs Commission, North Dakota

facts.text: As of July 2024, an estimated 33,276 members were enrolled in the Turtle Mountain Band.

source.title: Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa | Indian Affairs Commission, North Dakota

nations.name: Absentee Shawnee Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma
nations.lands: central Oklahoma, including the Shawnee and Little Axe areas

facts.text: The Tribe's government page describes separate Legislative/Executive and Judicial branches, alongside an independent Election Commission.

source.title: Government | Absentee Shawnee Tribe
source.publisher: Absentee Shawnee Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma
